lines.text: In the servants’ hall there is a board of bells, numbered one to five. When a bell rings, everyone knows exactly who is wanted.
Clara’s fingers, the Butler explains, work the same way.
Now, at the piano. Hold up both hands. Ask someone to call a number, and wiggle that finger on both hands.
And here is how it ended.
Fingers were not always numbered this way. In old English music the thumb was marked with a cross, and the fingers were 1, 2, 3, 4.
The way you learn, thumb as 1, won in the end.
One more thing to try. Play C D E F G with your right hand, saying the numbers. Then say them the old English way: cross, 1, 2, 3, 4.
Then the Butler handed her the key to the next floor. “Mind the Queen,” he said. “And whatever you do, do not sit in the King’s chair.”
